To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the DMA block of DMA(x)MCP30 copolymers is responsible for DNA condensation and that the PC-based block acts as a biologically compatible steric stabilizer.
the morphologies of the DNA complex obtained using DMA(x)Mpc30 (where the MPC block was kept constant) are different when studied in vacuo by TEM and in aqueous medium by AFM.
the morphologies of the DNA complexes obtained using DMA(x)Mpc30 copolymers, studied by TEM and AFM, are different.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel phosphorylcholines as a new generation of gene delivery vectors.
the development of novel biocompatible gene delivery vectors, which have the capacity to condense DNA into a highly ordered structure, which is also able to protect the DNA from enzymatic attack.
the development of new synthetic gene delivery materials that can condense and protect the DNA from enzymatic degradation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

DNA complexation by DMA(x)MCP30 copolymers leads to a variety of different morphologies depending on the DMA block length, which are different in vacuo and in aqueous medium, and that these morphologies are not necessarily related to the protection of the DNA against enzymatic degradation.
the copolymers DMA(x)MCP30 condense DNA more efficiently than the DMA homopolymeric counterpart.
the copolymers with a DMA degree of polymerization greater than 10 are capable of condensing DNA effectively and protecting it from enzymatic degradation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the highly condensed structures observed by AFMs are the in vitro morphologies of the DNA complexes, while the loosely condensed structures observed by TEM are more likely the in vivo morphologies of these complexes.
the DMA block is the main component responsible for the DNA condensation process, whereas the hydrophilic MPC block is the main determinant for the morphology of the DNA complex in solution.

the copolymer DMA(x)MCP30 series is a promising vector candidate for in vivo applications, and the combination of AFM and TEM is a powerful tool for understanding the mechanism of DNA condensation and protection.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the DMA-MPC copolymer series can condense DNA efficiently, with the morphology depending on the DMA block length, as determined by AFM and TEM, but the DMA homopolymeric complex provides the best DNA protection against enzymatic attack.
the highly hydrophillic nature of the MPC moiety in the DMA(x) MPC30 copolymer system results in different morphologies of DNA condensation when studied by TEM and AFM.
the DMA-MPC copolymer series can effectively condense DNA into highly condensed structures, which are similar to other well-known cationic polymers.
